verifier_note: Checked all 53 warrant sources by direct retrieval (17 dated 'Announcing Rust 1.NN.0' posts 1.80-1.98, 3 topic blog posts, the current edition guide's 2024 chapter across 12 pages, the current rustc book and Cargo book, current std/core docs, and two RELEASES.md snapshots) plus roughly 20 uncited 'stabilized in 1.NN' claims scattered through gotchas (LazyCell 1.80, Vec::extract_if 1.87, array_windows 1.94, Box::new_zeroed 1.92, assert_matches! 1.96, cargo info 1.82, publish --workspace 1.90, build.build-dir/--target host-tuple 1.91, resolver.lockfile-path 1.97, cargo fix target-selection 1.89, dangerous_implicit_autorefs added-1.88/deny-1.89, etc.) via independent search. Also ran every check in checks[] myself through scripts/compile_oracle.py against the real pinned rustc 1.98.1 (host, wasm32-unknown-unknown and wasm32v1-none): 58/58 passed. Also checked every engine_note claim against si-rpg-engine@main via gh api (lib.rs, rapier_law.rs, Cargo.toml, .cargo/config.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, build.mjs) byte-for-byte, including all 7 static_mut_refs line numbers and all 10 #[no_mangle] export names. Result: zero source misattributions, zero stale APIs, zero check/prose mismatches, zero wrong engine facts across all 10 recipes. Systemic weakness: this lane's two verification paths (citation retrieval and the compile oracle) both have a blind spot the recipes exploit unintentionally — precise-looking measured numbers in gotchas that are neither cited nor exercised by any checks[] entry. Recipe 4's gotcha claims the relaxed-simd fused-multiply-add 'returned the fused result... (-8.67e-19 where a separate multiply and add give 0)', but check #6 in that same recipe only asserts the function compiles and exports 'fused' — it never asserts that stdout value, so the specific number is untested by the very check sitting next to it. Recipe 1's gotchas cite exact digest prefixes and a '22 bytes' delta from a blank-line probe with no matching check and no source at all. These are plausible (spec text for algebraic_*/relaxed-simd explicitly allows codegen-dependent results, so the shape of the claim is right) but unfalsifiable by anyone reading only this lane's artifacts; they rest entirely on an unlogged local run.
